scope: Project-run onboarding, editorial and UI regression checks. No outside users, new Lighthouse score, human listening or every-frame certification.

static_mobile.scope: Production build navigation: no irrelevant API requests/subscriptions and no horizontal overflow. This is not a Lighthouse or physical-phone measurement.

pitch.artwork: No generated conceptual illustrations. Actual product captures have dated provenance; screenshots remain raster images.
coverage: actual two-client withdrawal and separate root test
working AI reference and India tools

remaining_gaps: One configured RPC supplies unseen-history completeness; no independent state/non-omission proof.
No unaided outside integration or established ecosystem moat.
Small separate root-update demo; no production migration or automatic policy rotation.
Mobile performance scores are historical simulated lab results, not physical devices or field INP.

hosted_ui.scope: Owned live domain. Actual MP4 playback/seeking and deck/package downloads; overview/SDK interactions and 390px layout. The SDK UI fixture and clipboard remain stubbed in its interaction case; real npm/RPC checks are separate receipts.

hosted_release.scope: Project-run final deployment smoke checks. Two current refused reads supplement the separately recorded actual before/after lifecycle. No new withdrawal was published by this script.

npm_production_audit.scope: npm audit --omit=dev on this checkout; not an audit of arbitrary applications.

editorial_refresh.scope: Static presentation and documentation refresh. All eight final PPTX and PDF pages reviewed, native table/chart and package structure validated. Existing unit and performance counts remain historical; not rerun for this media-only change.

google_slides_review.application: Google Slides in Chrome, actual authenticated browser UI
google_slides_review.correction: Chart axis headroom prevents two 98 labels being clipped after Google conversion. Values and historical scope unchanged.
google_slides_review.conversion_limitations: Google imports the chart as a raster image and may round its display axis to120. Original PPTX retains its native editable chart/workbook; the comparison table and narrative text remain editable in Slides.
